notes:
**Windows** — run `ruze_0.0.22_x64-setup.exe`.
**Linux** — `flatpak install ruze-0.0.22.flatpak`, then `flatpak run com.ruze.chat`.
**Android** — sideload `ruze-0.0.22.apk`. arm64 devices, Android 8.0 or newer.

---

### Added

- **The server rail says when somebody is in a voice channel.** You had to be
  looking at a server to find out anyone was talking in it. The dot on a
  server's icon now turns green and carries a small speaker whenever somebody
  is in one of its voice channels — including servers you have not opened, so a
  room filling up is visible from wherever you are. It takes the place of the
  connection dot rather than sitting beside it: you cannot be in a call without
  being connected, so the two could never disagree.

- **Turn somebody down from the voice list.** Right-clicking a name in a voice
  channel — in the sidebar or in the room itself — now opens their volume
  slider along with their profile. It was only reachable through the profile
  dialog before, which is the wrong place for it: turning somebody down is
  something you do while they are talking, and the slider should not be three
  clicks and a dialog away while you listen to them at the wrong volume. The
  menu stays open while you drag, and the setting is the same one the profile
  card shows.

- **Reactions in a friend conversation.** Reacting was something you could
  only do in a server channel; a direct conversation had no way to answer a
  message without writing one. Hover a message and the smiley is there, the
  same as in a channel.

  Worth knowing how it works, because a conversation is not one shared
  document but two one-way ones — each of you can only write to your own half.
  A reaction therefore lives in the half belonging to whoever left it, and what
  you see under a message is both halves read together. That is also what makes
  one unforgeable: an entry is signed, in its author's own document, so there
  is no way to react as somebody else. The practical consequence is the same as
  for a message — a reaction reaches the other person when you are both online,
  not before.

- **An emoji sent on its own is drawn large, and moves.** A message that is
  nothing but emoji is a gesture rather than a sentence, so it is now rendered
  at a size to match and animated using Google's Noto set — in a channel and in
  a friend conversation, where it also loses the bubble behind it, because the
  emoji is the message. Emoji inside a sentence are unchanged, and so are
  reactions.

  This is the one thing Ruze fetches from anyone but the people you are talking
  to, so it is bounded on purpose: each emoji is downloaded at most once ever
  on a device and then kept, so a channel where everyone posts 🎉 is a single
  request rather than one per message. Emoji with no animation — flags,
  families, keycaps — are noted as such and never asked about twice. There is a
  switch in Settings → Emoji, on by default; turned off, nothing is ever
  requested and a lone emoji is still drawn large, just without the movement.

- **Emoji are drawn half again as large.** An emoji fills its whole line box
  where a letter only fills the cap height, so at the size of the text around
  it one reads noticeably smaller than it should. Emoji in a message, on a
  reaction pill, and every selectable one in the picker are now a step and a
  half up.

- **Reactions sit on the message instead of under it.** Each one was a filled
  chip drawn in the same shade as the composer, so a row of them read as
  controls parked beneath the message rather than as something the message had
  collected — and hovering the message made them detach, because the row
  changed colour and the chips did not. They are now just the emoji and its
  count, tucked up against the message and lined up with its first letter. The
  pill appears under the pointer, which is when it matters that it is a button.
  Ones you pressed keep a faint tint, so a glance still finds them.

- **Emoji in the message box, everywhere there is one.** The picker only ever
  opened to react to something somebody else had written; there was no way to
  put an emoji in a message you were writing. There is a smiley beside the box
  now, in a channel and in a friend conversation both, and what it inserts
  lands at the cursor rather than at the end of the line.

- **A copy button on the pairing code.** Adding another device shows a QR to
  scan and the same code as text underneath, for the pairing where nothing has
  a camera pointed at anything. Getting that text across meant selecting three
  wrapped lines of it by hand; there is now a Copy beside it.

### Changed

- **GIF search works without setting anything up, and only searches KLIPY.**
  A release now carries a KLIPY key, so the picker finds reaction GIFs the
  first time it is opened rather than asking for a key first. The Openverse
  fallback is gone with it — it needed no key, but it searched Creative
  Commons illustrations rather than reactions, which is not what anybody opens
  a GIF picker for.

  The key that ships is shared by every copy of Ruze, so its hourly search
  limit is shared too. Settings still takes a key of your own, which overrides
  it and gets its own allowance; keys are free from klipy.com/developers.

- **A friend conversation lays its messages out better.** Each bubble put the
  timestamp on a line of its own, so a two-word message was a tall box. The
  time now sits beside the bubble, in the space the bubble leaves empty — to
  the right of one of theirs, to the left of one of yours — and reactions hang
  under the bubble rather than inside it. Which side a message sits on is
  unchanged.

- **Bigger type on Android.** The interface was sized for a desktop monitor,
  and on a phone held in the hand it read a size too small. The whole Android
  UI — text, spacing, avatars and icons together — now scales up one step.
  Desktop is unchanged.

### Fixed

- **Reacting to a message near the top of the window no longer locks the app
  up.** The emoji picker works out where to sit once it knows its own size,
  and the step that folds it below the click when there is no room above it
  read back the position it had just written. That made the calculation depend
  on its own result, so the two placements took turns forever and the window
  stopped responding. The same shape has been taken out of the right-click
  menu, where it needed a window too small to hit in practice.

- **The cursor stays in the message box after you send.** In a direct
  message the box switched itself off while the message was in the air, and
  switching off the thing you are typing in hands focus back to the page — so
  every Enter cost you the cursor and the next message started with a click.
  The box stays live now, in conversations and channels both, and the keyboard
  stays up on a phone.
